hypothesis.screened_against_target: no — this is a tool-behaviour claim, not a codegen one; it was read out of probe.py's revert branch at 6c2e07f78 and not exercised end to end.
hypothesis.statement: probe's `--revert` path carries the SAME defect item 5 fixed in `--discard`: when the banked snapshot IS the working tree it prints `nothing to restore: <snapshot> IS the current working tree` and then FALLS THROUGH to an ordinary re-score, so it exits 0 having restored nothing. It was left alone because its exit code carries the VERDICT's meaning (conflict_gate writes it), so the fix needs a decision about what a verdict-bearing exit code means for a restore that declined — not the one-line change --discard took.
